pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED READING : READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.8: Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we read texts with correct speed?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a text with correct speed and expression
2. apply appropriate intonation and stress when reading texts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED READING : READING COMPREHENSION
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED READING : READING COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a text with correct speed and expression

What this means
In this part you learn to read a text with correct speed and expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a text with correct speed and expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a text with correct speed and expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply appropriate intonation and stress when reading texts

What this means
In this part you learn to apply appropriate intonation and stress when reading texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply appropriate intonation and stress when reading texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply appropriate intonation and stress when reading texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a text with correct speed and expression)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension to a partner. (skill: apply appropriate intonation and stress when reading texts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a text with correct speed and expression.
3. Practise this skill: apply appropriate intonation and stress when reading texts.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we read texts with correct speed?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Reading : Reading Comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a text with correct speed and expression.
5. Be able to: apply appropriate intonation and stress when reading texts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
